extracted.intended_audience: educational institutions' Title IX coordinators, administrators, and legal counsel (K-12 and postsecondary)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for educational institutions to design and implement Title IX grievance procedures, including evidence access, credibility assessment, burdens and safeguards, standards of proof, FERPA interaction, and appeals. Applies to elementary, secondary, and postsecondary recipients with room for recipient-specific flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence access options
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide each party an equal opportunity to access evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible by either (a) providing access to the evidence, or (b) providing an accurate description of such evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the recipient initially chooses to provide an accurate description and then a party requests access to the evidence, the recipient must provide access. Both the evidence option and the description option require the recipient to give the parties a reasonable opportunity to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable opportunity to respond to evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must provide parties a reasonable opportunity to respond to the evidence or to the accurate description of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasonableness requires that parties can meaningfully respond and accommodates the nature and volume of evidence; the opportunity generally takes place at the end of the investigation after evidence is gathered, but recipients may permit responses at other points. The Department declines to list fixed examples, leaving reasonableness to recipient judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing and addressing unauthorized disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to prevent and address a party's unauthorized disclosure of information and evidence obtained solely through the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: What is reasonable may vary by circumstances — from informing parties of expectations and consequences for disclosure to using software that restricts redistribution. Disclosures for purposes of administrative proceedings or litigation related to the complaint of sex discrimination are authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with FERPA (education records disclosures)
rubrics_metrics.description: Title IX requirements to disclose evidence relevant and not otherwise impermissible may involve education records under FERPA; where Title IX disclosure requirements conflict with FERPA, the constitutional override and the GEPA override apply to require disclosure to parties and advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FERPA defines 'education records' and parents/eligible students have inspection rights, but Title IX disclosure obligations can require sharing information that might not otherwise be disclosed under FERPA. Nothing in Title IX derogates parents' legal rights to act on behalf of a student (see §106.6(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Process for evaluating allegations and assessing credibility (§106.45(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to create a process for assessing the credibility of parties and witnesses when credibility is both in dispute and relevant to evaluating one or more allegations of sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required process must enable the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses to adequately assess credibility; mere review of evidence is not sufficient. Recipients have discretion to design the process, taking into account due process, administrative structure, education community, and applicable law. The requirement applies to all complaints of sex discrimination, not limited to sex-based harassment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker questioning (not required party questioning)
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations require that the process for assessing credibility enables the decisionmaker to question parties and witnesses rather than requiring parties themselves to conduct questioning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may nevertheless permit party-submitted written questions or use other processes (including live hearings) if they choose. The rule was designed to avoid imposing a quasi-legal process on recipients, especially K-12, while still providing a meaningful opportunity to be heard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility on live hearings and cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients (including elementary and secondary schools) are not required to hold live hearings or permit questioning by an advisor; they may choose live hearings or other processes appropriate to their educational environment and applicable law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department maintains flexibility so K-12 recipients can avoid live hearings where inappropriate due to age/development, but recipients may choose live hearings (e.g., for older students or where state law requires them). Postsecondary procedures for sex-based harassment involving student parties remain governed by §106.46(g) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary relevance and impermissible evidence limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any questions a decisionmaker asks and any evidence considered must comply with the evidentiary standard applicable to all evidence in the grievance procedures: that evidence be relevant and not otherwise impermissible under §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions that could be traumatizing or irrelevant must still satisfy the relevance/impermissibility test; recipients must exclude types of evidence declared impermissible by the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof (preponderance unless consistent alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must use the preponderance of the evidence standard to determine whether sex discrimination occurred unless the recipient uses the clear and convincing evidence standard in all other comparable proceedings, in which case it may elect clear and convincing for sex discrimination cases as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department retained the July 2022 NPRM standard: preponderance by default, with the option to use clear and convincing only if that standard is used consistently in all comparable proceedings. The Department considered judicial precedent and procedural safeguards in reaching this position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable treatment of complainants and respondents
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must treat complainants and respondents equitably.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a foundational requirement (§106.45(b)(1)) and underpins other procedural safeguards to ensure fairness across investigative and adjudicative steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion to dismiss complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients have discretion to dismiss a complaint in four specified circumstances, including when allegations, even if proven, would not constitute sex discrimination under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients also must provide the right to appeal the dismissal (§106.45(d)(3)). Dismissal is distinct from merits determinations and must be handled in accord with the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to parties of allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide notice to the parties of the allegations being investigated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice requirements are codified at §106.45(c) to ensure parties are informed of the complaint details and able to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions only after procedures and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient's grievance procedures must be followed before the imposition of any disciplinary sanctions against a respondent, and sanctions may be imposed only if it is determined that the respondent engaged in prohibited sex discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §§106.45(h)(3) and (h)(4); procedural compliance is necessary prior to sanctioning to ensure fairness and legal sufficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and exclusion of impermissible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must conduct an objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and must exclude certain types of evidence deemed impermissible by the regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements located at §§106.45(b)(6) and (7) ensure evidence is weighed impartially and that specified categories of evidence are not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden on recipient to investigate and gather sufficient evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient bears the burden to conduct an investigation that gathers sufficient evidence to reach a determination about whether sex discrimination occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This places the obligation on the institution rather than on the parties to assemble the evidentiary record (§106.45(f)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to present witnesses and evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must be provided an equal opportunity to present fact witnesses and other inculpatory and exculpatory evidence that are relevant and not otherwise impermissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §106.45(f)(2); recipients must ensure parity in the ability to call witnesses and offer evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal opportunity to access evidence and to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party must be provided an equal opportunity to access evidence that is relevant and not otherwise impermissible and a reasonable opportunity to respond to that evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates and emphasizes parity in evidence access and response rights under §106.45(f)(4); see also the specific evidence access options and timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker impartiality and avoidance of conflicts/bias
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias for or against complainants or respondents generally or an individual complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §106.45(b)(2); impartiality is a core safeguard to reliable outcomes and due process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of non-responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Grievance procedures must include a presumption that the respondent is not responsible for the alleged conduct until a determination is made at the conclusion of the recipient's grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codified at §106.45(b)(3); this presumption protects respondents during the investigatory and adjudicative process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy protections for parties and witnesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must take reasonable steps to protect the privacy of the parties and witnesses during the grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §106.45(b)(5) — privacy protections are required though not absolute; they are balanced with disclosure/access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker training requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisionmakers must receive training on how to serve impartially, including avoiding prejudgment of the facts at issue, conflicts of interest, and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training requirements are set out in §106.8(d) and are intended to reduce biased outcomes and ensure competence in applying the regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals: minimum parity and specified bases
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient must offer parties an appeal that, at minimum, is the same as it offers in all other comparable proceedings; postsecondary institutions must offer an appeal based on procedural irregularity or bias or conflict of interest by the decisionmaker that would change the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See §§106.45(i) and 106.46(i). Postsecondary institutions may offer additional appeal bases equally to all parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient may adopt additional provisions if applied equally (§106.45(j))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may adopt additional provisions as part of their grievance procedures provided any additional provisions apply equally to the parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This allows institutions flexibility to supplement procedures while maintaining parity and nondiscrimination among parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility to consider age, development, and local law in process design
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should consider the age and developmental level of students, their administrative structure, education community, and applicable state or local law when designing processes to comply with §106.45(g) and other requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department declines to prescribe specific methods, instead offering technical assistance; recipients in some jurisdictions may be constrained by state laws requiring certain procedures.
